full_judgment: 2. Plaintiff-respondent No. 1 instituted the aforesaid suit in the second Court of the Assistant Judge, Satkania, for permanent injunction alleging, inter alia, that the suit land measuring 3. 23 acres under R.S. Khatian No. 836 belonged to one Fazar Ali in Korfa right and the raiyati right thereof belonged to Emdad Ali. Fazar Ali got mortgaged the suit land to one Jebunnessa and Basharat Ali by a registered deed dated 23.7.1921 and inducted them into possession of the suit land. Emdad Ali filed a rent suit against the heirs of Fazar Ali and the kot-mortgagees and got decree on 28.7.1938. During the pendency of the rent suit widow of Fazar Ali on her own behalf and on behalf of some minor children of said Fazar Ali executed a yearly kabuliyat relationg to 1.61 acres out of the suit land on 29.6.1938 in favour of Nurddin, predecessor of the defendant-appellants. A case was filed before the Debt Settlement Board for releasing the said kot mortagage which was executed by said Fazar Ali. That case was pending even after the passing of the rent decree in favour of Emdad Ali. The rent decree could not be executed as it was stayed by the Debt Settlement Board. However, when the stay order was vacated, in the rent execution Case No.1225 of 1938 the tenancy was auction sold on 10.9.1956 and the predecessor of the plaintiff, one Abdul Latif purchased the same in auction and took delivery of possession on 5.1.1957 and also annulled the encumbrances under Section 167 of the Bengal Tenancy Act namely, the interest of said Nuruddin, predecessor of the appellants. The said Abdul Latif mutated his name and paid rent.
